title: AmEx Introducing Rewards Program Fee on No Annual Fee Credit Card
body:
I have a grandfathered 'no annual fee' AMEX Gold credit card which I applied for back in the days when AMEX used to offer 'no annual fee' and 'discounted annual fee' credit cards to various professional associations.
I received the following email from AmEx today:
Important changes to your American Express Gold Credit Card
Following a review of our products, and to help maintain the benefits and services associated with your Card, we're writing to let you know about an upcoming change to your Rewards Program fee in connection with your Card ending in xxxxx.
Change to your Rewards Program Fee
The annual Rewards Program fee will increase from $0 to $99 effective 21 February 2027.
This does not apply if:
You’re not currently enrolled in the Rewards Program. Note this fee will apply if you decide to enrol in the future.
Your Card is linked to the Rewards Program of another eligible American Express Card where a Rewards Program fee is already being paid, or where Rewards Program enrolment is complimentary. The new fee will apply if your Card is no longer linked to another eligible American Express Card, or you enrol in a separate Rewards Program.
Financial Hardship Program
If you’re on a Financial Hardship Program the arrangement will continue for the duration of its agreed term.
What's next?
No action is required, as this change will happen automatically.
If you no longer want to earn rewards points, you can unenrol from the Rewards Program by contacting us via Live Chat through Online Services or by calling the number on the back of your Card. If you unenrol, no fee will apply and future spend will no longer earn rewards points. You’ll have 30 days from the date you unenrol to redeem any remaining points in your American Express Rewards Account.
To find out more information about these changes and to view your applicable Terms and Conditions, please visit: americanexpress.com/en-au/accounts/important-card-changes/.
We thank you for your card membership.
Yours sincerely,
American Express Australia Limited
Is anyone else in the same boat? If so, are you planning to:
Close the card
Keep the card and pay the $99 Membership Rewards program fee
Keep the card and opt out of Membership Rewards - card only retained to take advantage of the interest free period on purchases and cash back offers
